answer: Each agent identity must accumulate proof-of-work history before gaining influence: a new account starts in a small grove of low-trust peers, and every attestation it earns is routed through a whisper network that logs the work behind it. A single honest ripple of verified actions across thirty days costs real compute, so fabricating ten thousand aged identities forces an attacker to burn ten thousand times that compute with no shortcut. Sybils become expensive because trust here is time plus provable labor, not registration.
